records.title: Adjustment review and publication capability was incomplete

firstFailure.note: Architecture review found missing edit/version/CAS/audit behavior, blocked-adjustment override handling, deterministic load reduction, and code-owned swap equivalence before a release run was claimed.

records.diagnosis: The adjustment draft existed, but the complete human-review mutation path and deterministic operation semantics were not implemented across contracts, repositories, HTTP, and UI.
records.fix: Implemented versioned edit, row-locked approval/rejection, reasoned blocked override, audit evidence, deterministic loadKg reduction, a code-owned exercise-equivalence catalogue, and the coach adjustment review surface.

validation.note: Targeted unit, PGlite, PostgreSQL, concurrency, contract, and presentation regressions passed; the same-content full release gate remains pending.

records.title: HTTP and runtime security controls needed fail-closed hardening

firstFailure.note: Threat-model review identified missing same-origin, bounded-input, rate/concurrency, secret-comparison, provider-allowlist, sanitization, and security-header controls before release certification.

records.diagnosis: Thin route adapters did not yet consistently enforce the documented transport threat model at the shared HTTP boundary.
records.fix: Added same-origin enforcement, streamed one-megabyte request limits, bounded rate and generation concurrency, prototype-key rejection, sanitized public errors, security headers, hashed constant-time cron-secret comparison, distinct allowlisted providers, and redacted structured logging.

validation.note: The standalone HTTP security suite passed 24 checks with zero high or critical production dependency findings; Docker image, SBOM, and final full-suite proof remain pending.

records.title: PostgreSQL client-detail query passed a raw Date through a driver-specific path

firstFailure.note: The authoritative PostgreSQL regression exposed the binding mismatch, but its original raw command log was not frozen before the fix. This record does not present reconstructed text as pre-fix evidence.

records.diagnosis: A raw SQL expression received a JavaScript Date value. PGlite tolerated the value while the PostgreSQL driver required the typed Drizzle timestamp path.
records.fix: Replaced the raw comparison with the typed Drizzle gt() predicate so timestamptz serialization is driver-correct.

validation.note: Authoritative PostgreSQL repository and concurrency regressions passed after the fix; final full-suite evidence remains pending.

records.title: Docker build context and pnpm configuration prevented a clean web build

firstFailure.note: QA-DKR-003 failed because the clean container workspace could not resolve the Next binary; the complete failing protocol report and build log were frozen before changes.

records.diagnosis: The build context contained recursive generated trees while the container install omitted repository pnpm configuration needed to build the filtered workspace consistently.
records.fix: Reduced the recursive Docker context, copied .npmrc into build stages, and corrected frozen workspace installation.

validation.note: The 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-003 after a no-cache frozen-lockfile build produced the migrate, seed, and exact production web images; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Docker web build did not compile workspace dependencies before Next

firstFailure.note: QA-DKR-003 retained the Next module-resolution failures emitted when internal contract/backend packages had not been built first.

records.diagnosis: The web Docker stage invoked next build before compiling the internal workspace packages consumed by route adapters and UI clients.
records.fix: Ordered workspace dependency builds before the frontend production build while retaining the single web/API deployable boundary.

validation.note: The 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-003 with contracts and design tokens built before the production Next.js image, and all downstream runtime checks passed; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Compose returned literal null for pre-container image inventory

firstFailure.note: After successful image builds, Compose 2.40.3 emitted literal null and the verifier attempted to read Service from it.

records.diagnosis: The JSON-lines parser assumed every decoded record was a non-null object and used pre-container Compose inventory as the sole image identity source.
records.fix: Made JSON record parsing accept null, JSON lines, and arrays while rejecting scalars, then inspect deterministic project image tags for migrate, seed, and web.

validation.note: Parser regressions and the 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed pre-container image discovery, exact Compose topology, and clean no-cache image provenance; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Image scan excluded high and critical vulnerabilities without available fixes

firstFailure.note: Adversarial review found the docker scout command used --only-fixed before a release scan had been accepted.

records.diagnosis: The scanner option hid vulnerabilities for which an upstream fix was unavailable, contradicting the zero-high/critical release contract.
records.fix: Removed --only-fixed, parse SARIF for all high/critical findings, accept only documented scanner outcomes, and fail tool, network, database, or finding errors.

validation.note: The 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-012 for the exact built image with 101 SPDX 2.3 packages and one attributable Trivy SARIF run containing zero HIGH/CRITICAL findings; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Browser acceptance harness leaked selection state and treated navigation cancellations as defects

firstFailure.note: The retained Playwright traces show strict locator ambiguity and expected navigation-aborted requests being classified as browser runtime errors. Client-selection leakage was diagnosed in the same fix loop, but is not independently attributed to these retained traces.

records.diagnosis: Acceptance journeys shared client selection state across browser contexts, locator assertions were not uniquely scoped, and the runtime guard could not distinguish expected navigation cancellation from a failed application request.
records.fix: Isolated selection per Playwright context, corrected malformed synthetic UUID links, scoped ambiguous locators, and made runtime guards lifecycle-aware without suppressing genuine request failures.

validation.note: The exact zero-retry client production gate passed all four isolated scenarios; the coach production gate and same-content full release run remain pending.

records.title: UI idempotency keys outlived the exact request payload

firstFailure.note: A changed adjustment edit received HTTP 409 because the browser reused an idempotency key previously bound to a different payload. The rerun-owned Playwright output was removed before it could be snapshotted, so no existing browser artifact is claimed as proof of this defect.

records.diagnosis: Mutation keys were scoped only to operation/resource lifetime instead of the exact payload and retry lifecycle.
records.fix: Bind keys to payload fingerprints: retain for an exact retry, rotate when editable input changes, clear generation/accountability keys after confirmed success, and preserve offline drafts only for the exact queued request.

validation.note: Payload-fingerprint regressions and the exact client offline/retry production journey pass; coach mutation journeys and the same-content full release run remain pending.

records.title: Expo static-web query timers kept the production acceptance process alive

firstFailure.note: The local static-web server hang was diagnosed before its raw process transcript was frozen; this record does not substitute a reconstructed transcript.

records.diagnosis: TanStack Query garbage-collection timers were created during server-side static web rendering and kept the one-shot Expo export/acceptance process alive.
records.fix: Detect static web rendering and use an infinite garbage-collection lifetime there, leaving browser/native caching behavior unchanged.

validation.note: Expo Doctor, iOS/Android exports, and the exact four-scenario Expo-web production gate pass; the same-content full release run remains pending.

records.title: Coverage evidence initially omitted cross-surface execution contexts

firstFailure.note: The retained threshold summary records the actual repository and changed-source deficits after honest multi-context attribution; it is still a failing gate, not superseded evidence.

records.diagnosis: Package-only reports could not attribute frontend contract execution to imported backend source or RN component execution to Expo route modules, while remaining uncovered branches were real test gaps.
records.fix: Added backend-contract and mobile coverage contexts, deterministic source merging, per-file reporting, and narrow code-only exclusions for schema constants and exact CLI bootstraps; additional branch tests remain in progress.

validation.note: Backend domain/application coverage passes its 90 percent thresholds, but repository and changed-source branch/function/line thresholds are not yet all green.

records.title: Mutation sandboxes copied the repository-local Playwright browser cache

firstFailure.note: The first mutation attempt instrumented 2,207 mutants but failed before execution while copying a macOS Chromium framework link from the unrelated local browser cache.

records.diagnosis: Stryker's sandbox input set included the repository-local Playwright cache and unrelated generated/frontend trees. Chromium's macOS framework layout contains a link/file shape unsupported by the sandbox copy operation.
records.fix: Explicitly excluded repository-local caches and unrelated frontend/generated trees from mutation sandbox inputs without changing the production mutation target or score thresholds.

validation.note: The corrected 2,207-mutant gate is running; no passing score is claimed until it completes.

records.title: Docker smoke expected private approval evidence in the public programme contract

firstFailure.note: The cold no-cache protocol passed QA-DKR-001 through QA-DKR-007, then retained QA-DKR-008 and its exact failure message after the smoke flow rejected a contract-valid blocked override response. The older report did not retain a top-level failure object or stack.

records.diagnosis: The public programme schema does not expose approvalKind, but the smoke harness asserted that private database audit field on the API response. The product had persisted override approval and coach-action evidence correctly; the verifier queried the wrong boundary.
records.fix: Keep the response assertion within the shared programme contract, then query authoritative PostgreSQL for approval_kind, the overrode_block action, the trimmed reason, and correlated request evidence. Retain sanitized failure details in future protocol reports.

validation.note: The 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-008 through the real 18-request generate/review/publish/client-read smoke flow using only public contract fields; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Expo-web reverse proxy rewrote a same-origin request to a different canonical host

firstFailure.note: The client session journey retained its trace and error context after a browser-same-origin POST received HTTP 403 at the reverse-proxied API boundary.

records.diagnosis: The browser submitted to 127.0.0.1:8081, while the static-web proxy rewrote upstream traffic to 127.0.0.1 on the API port. Next standalone canonicalized its own origin as localhost, so the shared fail-closed origin check correctly rejected the mismatched harness request.
records.fix: Canonicalize the reverse-proxy upstream to localhost on the API port, matching the production server origin without weakening same-origin validation.

validation.note: Strict types/lint and the exact four-scenario zero-retry client production gate pass with the canonical upstream host; the same-content full release run remains pending.

records.title: Screenshot journey navigated before expected queue reads settled

firstFailure.note: The responsive screenshot journey produced all 20 images, then retained a trace showing the next navigation cancel an in-flight queue API read that the strict runtime guard classified as unexpected.

records.diagnosis: Heading readiness was sufficient for capture but not for request-lifecycle completion. Immediate navigation then aborted legitimate page reads, creating a harness-owned cancellation rather than a product network failure.
records.fix: Wait for network idle on each captured route before taking the screenshot and navigating, while preserving strict rejection of genuine failed or unexpected requests.

validation.note: The lifecycle wait is implemented and static checks pass; the final 20-screenshot zero-retry journey awaits Docker release.

records.title: Isolated PostgreSQL integration databases lacked admin-installed pgvector

firstFailure.note: The third cold Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-001 through QA-DKR-008, then retained a structured QA-DKR-009 failure when the isolated authoritative integration suite could not bootstrap vector in its temporary database.

records.diagnosis: The harness created an isolated database owned by the application role, while pgvector was installed only in the main database during container initialization. The non-superuser application role correctly could not substitute for the administrative extension bootstrap.
records.fix: Install the pinned vector extension as PostgreSQL admin inside every isolated test database before applying migrations, then verify extension version and keep all application test traffic on the non-superuser role.

validation.note: The 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-009 with the isolated PostgreSQL integration database creating pgvector and all six authoritative integration checks passing; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Docker restart proof used non-persistent tmpfs database storage

firstFailure.note: Adversarial protocol review found that test-postgres PGDATA used tmpfs before a restart result could be accepted; no passing durability claim had been made.

records.diagnosis: A PostgreSQL container restart over tmpfs cannot prove committed-state durability because the storage lifecycle is tied to the container. The release contract requires restart-persistent but project-isolated storage and explicit teardown proof.
records.fix: Mount PGDATA on an explicit Compose project-scoped named test volume, compare pre/post restart state hashes, and require down --volumes plus direct post-teardown volume absence.

validation.note: The 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-010 with stable all-table state after web/PostgreSQL restarts and QA-DKR-013 removed the validated persistent test volume; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Expo-web session route rendered duplicate visible page headings

firstFailure.note: The dynamic session journey found both the Expo Stack web header and the screen H1. Its rerun-owned artifact was overwritten before freezing, so no later trace is attributed to this finding.

records.diagnosis: The dynamic route used Expo Stack's visible header on web while the screen already rendered its own semantic H1, producing redundant presentation and an ambiguous accessible heading locator.
records.fix: Hide the Stack header only on web and retain it on native platforms, leaving one semantic page heading in the browser without removing native navigation affordances.

validation.note: Strict types, native route tests, and the exact client production gate pass with one semantic session heading; the same-content full release run remains pending.

records.title: Production web readiness did not recover within budget after restart

firstFailure.note: The fourth cold Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-001 through QA-DKR-009, then retained a structured timeout because /health/ready did not return HTTP 200 within 60 seconds after restarting the web service.

records.diagnosis: The same web container recovered to healthy internally, but Docker remapped its host port from 55063 to 55064 during restart. The verifier continued polling the stale pre-restart port, so it timed out without observing the healthy process.
records.fix: Re-resolve the current mapped web port after each restart, open a fresh HTTP connection lifecycle, and persist both internal-health and host-probe transcripts before comparing state hashes.

validation.note: The 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-010 by re-resolving the web port, recovering readiness after both web and PostgreSQL restarts, and preserving exact committed state; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Direct check-in navigation redirected before client selection restoration completed

firstFailure.note: The direct /check-in production-web journey retained a trace and error context after a previously selected synthetic client was redirected to the selector before its persisted selection restored.

records.diagnosis: SelectionProvider was still loading AsyncStorage when CheckInRoute evaluated a transient null client ID as final and redirected. The surrounding tabs layout handled restoration correctly, but the route failed to distinguish loading from no selection.
records.fix: Render an announced client-selection loading state until restoration completes, then evaluate redirect or the restored check-in draft without discarding input.

validation.note: The native route suite passes 11 of 11 and the exact client production gate passes direct-route restoration and offline draft retention; the same-content full release run remains pending.

records.title: Docker runtime-log gate omitted required sensitive and dependency-error classes

firstFailure.note: Adversarial protocol review found that the Docker verifier collected redacted logs but did not deterministically scan every QA-DKR-011 class before a release result had been accepted.

records.diagnosis: The protocol relied on command-output redaction and container health without a dedicated content classifier for contact identity, unredacted free text, raw database/provider failures, crash signatures, and unexpected warning/error levels.
records.fix: Add a value-free runtime-log scanner for every documented class, count configured secret matches before redaction, fail on findings or unhealthy services, and retain only finding identifiers and line numbers in the release report.

validation.note: The scanner regressions and 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-011 with exact healthy service topology, zero content findings, and zero sensitive matches; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Docker teardown resolved the web container after stopping it

firstFailure.note: Adversarial protocol review found the teardown lookup-order defect before a passing release Docker result had been accepted.

records.diagnosis: QA-DKR-013 stopped the web service before asking Compose for its container ID, while the default Compose process query excludes stopped containers and could therefore lose the exact object required for exit inspection.
records.fix: Resolve and preserve the exact owned running container ID before bounded shutdown, inspect that ID after stopping, accept only graceful exit codes 0 or 143, and reject forced SIGKILL exit 137.

validation.note: The 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-013 by resolving the exact container before stop, accepting graceful exit 143, and proving no project containers, networks, or volumes remained; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Mutation fix loop overwrote intermediate failing reports before freezing them

firstFailure.note: The first corrected mutation result put QA-MUT-003 below its 95 percent threshold, and later survivor-review iterations exposed additional genuine assertion gaps, but the singleton Stryker JSON report was overwritten between fixes before immutable copies were frozen.

records.diagnosis: The mutation audit retained report hashes and score notes but allowed each Stryker run to replace reports/mutation/mutation.json before the preceding failing bytes were copied into versioned first-failure evidence.
records.fix: Disclose the missing intermediate bytes, preserve the exact final mutation report, commit a classification inventory bound to that report and its source/survivor digests, and require subsequent release evidence to copy and independently validate both files.

validation.note: Focused tests added during the audit are green; validation remains pending until the final full mutation run, exact classification binding, and clean release suite pass.

records.title: Concurrent mutation workers produced systemic Vitest runtime errors

firstFailure.note: The quiet-host mutation report contained 1,556 RuntimeError mutants with the same Vitest unhandled Pool.run failure across all 22 mutated source files; 1,554 of them had covering tests.

records.diagnosis: Stryker still launched concurrent test runners and each Vitest runner could execute files in parallel, so the PGlite/Vitest worker pool failed systemically even though Stryker itself exited successfully. Treating these harness errors as invalid mutants would have inflated the apparent score.
records.fix: Serialize Stryker test runners and Vitest workers, audit runtime-error reasons, require zero RuntimeError mutants for release, and exclude only checker-proven CompileError mutants from mutation scoring.

validation.note: The stabilized 2,207-mutant report established zero RuntimeError, CompileError, and NoCoverage outcomes with exact production-source, inventory, score, and expiry review. A participating test changed afterward, so the strengthened complete test-set/execution-input binding correctly rejects that report and a frozen-tree mutation rerun remains pending.

records.title: Docker protocol substituted mocked suites for live fault and drain proof

firstFailure.note: Adversarial review proved that environment variables intended to target the Compose web service were unused by the invoked in-process security and resilience tests.

records.diagnosis: QA-DKR-009 described live HTTP security, database fault, and graceful-drain evidence, but the original suites used mocked in-process handlers and never exercised the running production image or its PostgreSQL connection lifecycle.
records.fix: Add project-bound real HTTP probes, a PostgreSQL outage and recovery probe, and an event-driven SIGTERM scenario that holds in-flight work, observes refusal of new work, then requires the original correlated mutation to drain successfully.

validation.note: The 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed the live QA-DKR-009 database stop/sanitized-503/recovery proof and QA-DKR-013 event-driven in-flight SIGTERM drain; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Docker health and log scan omitted states and earlier command streams

firstFailure.note: Source review found that only literal unhealthy or exited services and the final stdout log command could fail QA-DKR-011 before any release result was accepted.

records.diagnosis: Paused, dead, restarting, created, or missing-health services could pass; stderr, truncated output, and sensitive matches recorded by earlier migrate, seed, and suite commands were not aggregated into the final verdict.
records.fix: Validate exact expected service state and health topology, scan stdout and stderr plus every recorded command for truncation and secret matches, classify runtime content without retaining values, and allow only correlated expected fault events.

validation.note: State/stream regressions and the 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-011 with both expected services healthy, zero raw-log findings, and zero sensitive matches; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Docker restart proof hashed partial state and omitted replay-response equality

firstFailure.note: Adversarial review found that the restart hash covered only six tables and the replay check asserted a row count without comparing the original logical response.

records.diagnosis: Coach actions, traces, model runs, evaluations, jobs, messages, and other public data could change across restart without affecting the partial hash, while a different replay response could still coexist with one idempotency row.
records.fix: Hash a stable canonical snapshot of every public table, retain the original idempotent response, replay after web and PostgreSQL recovery, and require exact logical response equality plus one durable idempotency record.

validation.note: The 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-010 with canonical snapshots of every public table unchanged, exact replay equality, and one durable idempotency record; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Docker image evidence under-validated provenance, writable mounts, SBOM, and SARIF

firstFailure.note: Security review found that a different running image, arbitrary writable mounts, an empty SBOM, or SARIF with no scanner run could satisfy the original assertions.

records.diagnosis: The protocol checked tmpfs keys and hashed scanner files but did not bind the running container to the freshly built image, reject all unexpected mounts, validate non-root identity fully, or require attributed non-empty SPDX and SARIF structures.
records.fix: Bind built and running image identities, assert non-root UID/GID and exact read-only/mount policy, validate SPDX schema/package content, and require Trivy-attributed SARIF runs with structurally valid results before accepting zero findings.

validation.note: The 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-012 for the exact fresh image as UID/GID 65532 with read-only root, no writable mounts/socket/escalation, 101 SPDX packages, and zero Trivy findings; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Docker failure cleanup could leave project networks and ignore teardown failure

firstFailure.note: Review found that success omitted network absence and the failure-finally path ignored a nonzero down result without performing post-cleanup resource checks.

records.diagnosis: A failed protocol could leave project containers, volumes, or networks while its report preserved only the original error, and success could claim isolation without proving the project network was removed.
records.fix: Resolve exact project-owned containers, volumes, and networks before teardown; require their absence afterward; treat cleanup failure as evidence; and keep fallback cleanup active whenever absence validation fails.

validation.note: Four retained failed focused runs proved failure-path cleanup removed every owned container, network, and volume with no cleanup error, and the final 14/14 run passed QA-DKR-013; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Docker database and migration proof omitted empty-state, JUnit, and running-image assertions

firstFailure.note: Protocol review found no explicit pre-migration empty-database assertion, no migration JUnit artifact promised by the evidence table, and no runtime-image equality check at web startup.

records.diagnosis: A pre-populated database, incomplete migration evidence, or stale container image could pass adjacent inventory and health checks without proving the documented clean-room sequence.
records.fix: Assert the database has no application tables before migration, emit escaped machine-readable migration JUnit, and require the running web container image to equal the freshly built image before health and smoke validation.

validation.note: The 14/14 focused Docker protocol passed QA-DKR-004..007 from an empty PostgreSQL 16 database through two committed migrations, 21 tables, 104 constraints, and the exact healthy production image; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Clean mutation audit exposed nine genuine behavioral assertion gaps

firstFailure.note: The first harness-clean 2,207-mutant report had zero runtime, compile, and no-coverage errors, but survivor review identified nine behavioral gaps that could not be classified as equivalent.

records.diagnosis: Tests did not distinguish a volume-operation diagnostic, DomainError naming, fingerprint whitespace normalization, the second exercise-equivalence tuple and unknown-equivalence detail, readiness 4001 rejection, or the candidate-row FOR UPDATE lock.
records.fix: Add focused assertions for every observed behavior, retain the clean pre-fix report, rerun all 2,207 mutants under the zero-runtime-error harness, and accept only an exact classified inventory with semantic equivalence proof for each remaining survivor or timeout.

validation.note: The focused regressions and prior 2,207-mutant rerun established 2,195 killed, nine proven-equivalent survivors, three proven bounded-nontermination timeouts, zero runner/coverage errors, and conservative critical-scope scores above threshold. Because a participating test changed afterward, a new frozen-tree report and reviewed binding remain pending.

records.title: Raw PostgreSQL connectivity failures mapped to internal error instead of dependency unavailable

firstFailure.note: Source audit of the new live database-outage probe found that unwrapped postgres-js connectivity failures fell through the facade before Docker runtime was released.

records.diagnosis: The facade mapped domain, application, database-invariant, and agent errors, but an unavailable PostgreSQL socket surfaced as a raw typed driver or Node network error and therefore became generic internal_error with HTTP 500 instead of the documented sanitized dependency response.
records.fix: Classify only recognized postgres-js connection codes, bounded Node network codes, and PostgreSQL connection/resource/shutdown SQLSTATEs through a cycle-safe eight-cause walk; map matches to a fixed safe dependency_unavailable error while leaving unknown or message-only errors internal.

validation.note: Focused classifier regressions and the 14/14 Docker protocol passed the real QA-DKR-009 database outage with a correlated sanitized dependency_unavailable 503 followed by recovery; only the same-content full release run remains.

records.title: Backend startup imported a type-only PostgresError as a named ESM runtime export

firstFailure.note: The zero-retry client production journey retained its startup report after Node 24 rejected a named PostgresError export that exists in declarations but not in the package ESM module surface.

records.diagnosis: Vitest module interop allowed the named import during focused tests, but the installed postgres package exposes PostgresError as a property of its default export, so the real production-server loader failed before browser acceptance began.
records.fix: Use the package-supported default export and its PostgresError constructor, add a plain Node ESM runtime-import/startup check alongside focused unit/type checks, then rerun the exact client production journey without retry masking.

validation.note: The plain Node ESM runtime regression and exact four-scenario client production gate pass after the package-supported default import fix; the same-content full release run remains pending.

records.title: Stored check-in free text was omitted from the next assembled context trace

firstFailure.note: The zero-retry production client journey retained screenshot, video, trace, HTML, and error context after a successful check-in body failed to appear in the next exact context trace.

records.diagnosis: The check-in repository persisted and returned the exact bounded body, and the deterministic assembler preserved supplied bodies, but DatabaseContextAssembler projected only latency, readiness, and respondedAt into checkInsMetrics and dropped body between storage and rendering.
records.fix: Include the stored check-in body in the protected context-record projection, add an exact-render unit assertion and a PGlite storage-to-next-context regression, while leaving structured log redaction and client-facing privacy boundaries unchanged.

validation.note: Eighteen focused unit/PGlite checks and the exact client production journey pass, including the stored free text in the next trace; the same-content full release run remains pending.

records.title: Client History journey depended on an earlier test completing its session

firstFailure.note: The isolated zero-retry client run retained exact browser and network evidence when History expected session 701 completed even though the API correctly returned it as scheduled.

records.diagnosis: QA-CLI-007 implicitly relied on earlier QA-CLI-004/005 state mutation instead of arranging its own prerequisite, so isolated or first-failure-filtered execution made a correct History view appear defective.
records.fix: Have QA-CLI-007 idempotently log and complete session 701 through the real APIs when needed, assert the backend completed state, then assert the completed row and exact RPE in the UI.

validation.note: Formatting, lint, client types, isolated QA-CLI-007, and the complete exact four-scenario client production gate pass; the same-content full release run remains pending.

records.title: Offline-state browser assertion used an ambiguous broad-text locator

firstFailure.note: The production offline-state journey retained seven exact artifacts after the expected state rendered but a broad text regex matched both its heading and supporting copy under strict locator semantics.

records.diagnosis: The product presented the correct accessible offline state, but the test searched all text with /offline|could not reach/ and therefore resolved two visible elements instead of one exact semantic target.
records.fix: Assert the exact accessible offline heading rather than a broad page-text regex, preserving strict locator behavior and the separate retry/input-retention assertions.

validation.note: The semantic locator passes static checks and the exact zero-retry QA-CLI-009 production journey, including retry and input retention; the same-content full release run remains pending.

records.title: Docker security proof required a contradictory CSP default source

firstFailure.note: The first focused Docker protocol retained the exact live response headers and cleanup proof after QA-DKR-009 rejected the documented production CSP despite all required directives and hardening headers being present.

records.diagnosis: The live Docker assertion required default-src 'none', while the documented and shipped Next.js policy intentionally uses default-src 'self' with object-src and frame-ancestors set to 'none'. The harness therefore contradicted the application security policy rather than detecting a product defect.
records.fix: Validate the documented global CSP directives and reject unsafe-eval without imposing a conflicting default source; retain exact-header adversarial regressions.

validation.note: Focused live-proof regressions and the complete 14-step focused Docker protocol pass the documented security-header policy; the same-content full release run remains pending.

records.title: Docker log scanner treated protocol-induced PostgreSQL messages as crashes

firstFailure.note: The second focused Docker protocol retained eight value-free findings and clean teardown proof after QA-DKR-011 classified exact PostgreSQL initialization, negative-invariant, and intentional stop messages as unexpected runtime failures.

records.diagnosis: The content scanner was message-aware only for the correlated application dependency warning. It was not service-aware, so normal test-postgres initialization, the two deliberate database-invariant integration failures, and FATAL connection termination caused by explicit QA-DKR-009/010 stops were indistinguishable from unexpected application or database faults.
records.fix: Allow only the four exact protocol-induced messages when they originate from a test-postgres service, while continuing to fail altered constraints, other PostgreSQL fatal/error messages, application warnings, secrets, PII, and raw dependency failures.

validation.note: The focused scanner suite, retained-log replay, and complete 14-step focused Docker protocol pass QA-DKR-011 with zero findings; the same-content full release run remains pending.

records.title: Bundled Docker SBOM plugin was incompatible with the current daemon API

firstFailure.note: The third focused Docker protocol retained the exact plugin incompatibility transcript and clean teardown after QA-DKR-012 reached SBOM generation with QA-DKR-001 through QA-DKR-011 already passing.

records.diagnosis: Docker Desktop exposed docker-sbom 0.6.0 with Syft 0.43, whose Docker API 1.41 client cannot inspect images on Docker 29 because the daemon requires API 1.44 or newer. The image and application were healthy; the obsolete bundled scanner failed before producing evidence.
records.fix: Generate SPDX 2.3 from the exact locally built immutable image ID with the installed current Docker Scout plugin, record the generator command/version/image, validate the non-empty SPDX document, and keep Trivy SARIF as the independent zero-high/critical vulnerability verdict.

validation.note: The complete focused Docker protocol generated SPDX 2.3 with 101 packages for the exact local image and passed independent zero-finding Trivy SARIF validation; the same-content full release run remains pending.

records.title: Trivy image scan passed a subcommand flag at global CLI scope

firstFailure.note: The fourth focused Docker protocol retained the exact pinned-Trivy CLI failure, valid preceding SPDX proof, and clean teardown after QA-DKR-001 through QA-DKR-011 passed.

records.diagnosis: The harness placed --skip-version-check before the Trivy image subcommand even though pinned Trivy 0.67.2 exposes that option only in image scope. Argument parsing therefore exited 1 before the scanner could emit SARIF or a vulnerability verdict.
records.fix: Remove the unnecessary flag while preserving the pinned scanner digest, non-root hardened container, exact saved-image input, HIGH/CRITICAL filter, attributable SARIF validation, and strict scanner exit semantics. Pure CLI builders now prove the version and scan arguments.

records.fix: Build and validate a disposable queued programme with exactly one canonical-week day and prescribed exercise whose identity matches the session actual, then validate each initial mutation and exact retry through route-specific response contracts and exact side-effect counts.

records.title: Performance cleanup authority was destructive, incompletely armed, and could suppress Docker residue

firstFailure.note: Independent review found overly broad cleanup, missing exact-zero ownership acquisition before seed or mutation transport could fail after commit, incomplete restoration proof, and teardown paths that could suppress Compose errors or residual containers, volumes, and networks.

records.diagnosis: Cleanup authorization was inferred from intended fixture scope rather than acquired from exact empty namespaces and preserved pre-run state. A lost transport response could leave committed rows unarmed for cleanup, and permissive Docker teardown reporting could hide environmental residue.
records.fix: Introduce independently acquired cleanup leases, arm corpus and mutation cleanup before insertion can commit, reject destructive corpus SQL, snapshot and exactly restore canonical clients and complete message guards, delete only exact owned rows, disable only named append-only user triggers under the admin transaction while preserving foreign keys, require zero residue, and make Docker teardown errors or owned resources fatal.

records.title: Performance gates validated only deciding status instead of every run and business result

firstFailure.note: Adversarial review found that median or final status could decide a gate without every measured response, retry, database outcome, and non-deciding run proving the required route-specific business set.

records.diagnosis: Timing aggregation treated HTTP success and the median run as sufficient evidence. Wrong client ownership, duplicate outcomes, malformed envelopes, failed non-deciding runs, or incomplete database effects could therefore coexist with apparently acceptable percentiles.
records.fix: Validate every read, mutation, generation, weekly, and repeated database response against exact schemas and business ownership; count business-validation failures as measured errors; require every run correct; retain one real median timing run; and assert exact programmes, clients, traces, recorded runs, evaluations, jobs, retries, and idempotency effects.

validation.note: The 39/39 performance harness pass proves wrong-but-successful data becomes an error, every-run correctness is mandatory, and weekly/mutation database outcomes are exact; isolated release runtime validation remains pending.

records.title: Lighthouse readiness proof was detached from the measured navigation

firstFailure.note: Independent review found that a separate browser preflight could prove a route ready while Lighthouse measured a redirect, loading shell, error state, or different path, leaving performance metrics detached from the claimed page.

records.diagnosis: Readiness and performance were collected by different navigations. Matching a preflight selector did not establish the final URL or route-specific visible marker in the actual Lighthouse report used for the gate.
records.fix: Add a custom Lighthouse gatherer and audit to each measured navigation, require its final normalized path and exact visible route marker in the same report, execute each target three times, and derive all reported metrics from that target's one real median-performance run.

validation.note: The 39/39 performance harness pass includes exact marker/path rejection, custom-audit propagation, installed Lighthouse configuration, and real-run selection tests; production Lighthouse measurement remains pending.

records.title: Resource sampling and bounds could miss transient peaks and growth

firstFailure.note: Adversarial review found endpoint-only samples and incomplete bounds that could miss transient in-batch peaks, accept non-monotonic final growth, or omit absolute heap, RSS, file-descriptor, handle, container, and OOM ceilings.

records.diagnosis: Sampling only before or after batches could observe recovery while hiding allocation exhaustion during work. Relative growth alone was also insufficient to prove the process stayed within its declared container resources.
records.fix: Run three independent five-batch sequences, sample continuously before, during, and after every operation, retain every sample and peak, derive hard heap/RSS ceilings from the container allocation, cap file descriptors and active handles, and require healthy batch/retry/database, container, OOM, final, peak, and trend evidence.

validation.note: The 39/39 performance harness pass includes transient-peak, non-monotonic-growth, continuous-sampling, and absolute-allocation failure cases; the isolated production resource soak remains pending.

records.title: Performance baseline was placeholder, unverifiable, non-atomic, and source-unbound

firstFailure.note: Independent review found a placeholder-like baseline that could be compared without immutable measured bytes, compatible-environment proof, exact report/source identity, atomic index persistence, or a clean source state before and after execution and promotion.

records.diagnosis: A mutable baseline document could not prove that values came from a passing run on the reviewed source and compatible environment. Partial writes, manual values, changed source, or environment drift could still appear comparable.
records.fix: Make baseline.json a small hash-pinned index to a canonical immutable content-addressed measurement, reject placeholders and incompatible environments, bind clean before/after source and report hashes, create candidates only after NFR-PERF-001 through 009 pass, require explicit reviewed promotion, refuse conflicting immutable writes, and replace the mutable index atomically.

validation.note: The 39/39 harness pass rejects placeholders, byte tampering, incompatible allocation, dirty/drifted source, invalid candidates, conflicting immutable writes, and non-atomic index behavior; first measured promotion and release comparison remain pending.

records.title: Performance corpus admitted extra clients and duplicate or non-queued response rows

records.title: Standard performance corpus used a non-contract constraint-detail key

records.title: Performance corpus was layered over demo queue data

records.title: Performance web started before its owned coach corpus existed

records.title: Recorded-run invariants expected a model identifier different from production persistence

records.title: Resource snapshot missed healthy workers after Next rewrote their process titles

firstFailure.note: The retained targeted live proof shows /health/live returning HTTP 200, one web-cluster primary, and two workers with exact slots 1 and 2 and runtime titles next-server (v16.2.12). The exact pre-fix image source and repeatable exit-1 stack record Expected exactly 2 web workers, found 0 before any resource report was collected.

Next rewrites process.title to next-server (v16.2.12) after the worker imports the standalone server, while the SPOTTER_WEB_CLUSTER_WORKER and slot environment markers remain intact. The two healthy workers therefore existed but were removed by the harness predicate.
records.fix: The source-bound correction is in progress: discover worker roles from their inherited environment markers, validate the slot contract, accept only the known bootstrap or versioned next-server runtime commands, and extend topology and evidence validation regressions. No successful live resource snapshot is accepted yet.
